airport.title: At the Airport
airport.subtitle: Get from the arrival gate to the city with confidence.
airport.culture: Chinese airports are big and busy; signs are bilingual, but announcements are usually only in Chinese. Taxis queue outside the arrivals hall, and most cities now have metro lines connecting the airport to downtown.

customs.title: Border Control & Customs
customs.subtitle: Answer the officer's questions and pass through immigration.
customs.culture: At Chinese border control you'll need your passport and possibly an arrival card. Travelers with nothing to declare usually take the green channel; answers are expected to be short and honest.

hotel-checkin.title: Hotel Check-in
hotel-checkin.subtitle: Register with your passport and get your room key.
hotel-checkin.culture: Chinese hotels usually hold your passport at check-in to register you with the police. Check-out time is often 12 noon, and even budget hotels commonly include breakfast.

hotel-service.title: Hotel Room Service
hotel-service.subtitle: Ask for towels, hot water or a wake-up call.
hotel-service.culture: Most Chinese hotels provide free bottled water and clean towels daily. A wake-up call (叫早) is free; some hotels also ask for a small cash deposit (押金) at check-in.

sim-card.title: Buying a SIM Card
sim-card.subtitle: Get a local data plan with your passport.
sim-card.culture: By law you must show your passport to buy a Chinese SIM card. China Mobile, China Unicom and China Telecom are the main carriers; airport kiosks and mall shops also sell tourist data cards.

wifi.title: Wi-Fi & Portable Hotspot
wifi.subtitle: Get online at a cafe or rent a pocket Wi-Fi.
wifi.culture: Many cafes and hotels offer free Wi-Fi, but some require a Chinese phone number to receive a login code. Renting a pocket Wi-Fi (随身Wi-Fi) at the airport is popular with short-term visitors.

luggage-storage.title: Luggage Storage
luggage-storage.subtitle: Leave your bags at a station, airport or hotel.
luggage-storage.culture: Train stations, airports and many malls have luggage storage counters or lockers. Keep the pickup ticket safe — you need it to collect your bags. Some hotels store luggage for free after check-out.

ask-direction.title: Asking for Directions
ask-direction.subtitle: Find your way on the street.
ask-direction.culture: Chinese locals are usually happy to help lost visitors, though many speak little English. Showing your hotel's Chinese address card or a map on your phone makes communication much easier.

check-out.title: Hotel Check-out & Invoice
check-out.subtitle: Leave the hotel and get a receipt.
check-out.culture: Asking for an invoice (发票) is common in China, especially for business travelers — you can have it made out to your name or a company. Check your room carefully before leaving.

lost-items.title: Lost & Found
lost-items.subtitle: Report a lost item and freeze your cards.
lost-items.culture: If you leave something in a taxi, call the company or ride-hailing hotline with your trip details. For a lost passport, contact your embassy; for bank cards, call the bank hotline to freeze them at once.
